incumbent_comparison: v003 is the best current review candidate because the exposed bay improves close-range quality, proportion and scale fidelity; at the identical 64-inch gameplay camera it is not materially more readable than v002, and the 330-inch room view remains inconclusive.
next_action_hypothesis: Backlog this approved-target episode after its third bounded attempt. If the workshop is revisited under a new target episode, prioritize a stronger large-scale work-bay silhouette and remove the residual cog cue; do not add a fourth candidate to this episode.

observations.art_direction_fit: The salvage appliance panels and open work bay fit the Scavenger brief; remove the bright cog cue in any future target episode.
observations.close_up_quality: The open bay, bench and supported roof are clearer in the 27.7-inch view; target-level surface richness and small crafted joins are still missing.
observations.gameplay_readability: Luna rates this 3/5. At the matched 64-inch view v003 does not read materially better than v002; work bay details and tools remain small.
observations.geometric_detail: The close view exposes the bench, shelves and rear tool wall more clearly than v002; small tools remain too small at settlement distance.
observations.material_realism: Broad baked enamel and galvanized color variation separates the reused materials, while the overall finish remains simpler than the approved concept.
observations.proportion: Godot validates the asset at 25.90 by 19.16 by 19.36 inches, within the intended 26 by 20 by 20 inch envelope.
observations.scale_fidelity: The local envelope passes technical bounds. In the 330-inch room overview the structure remains too small for a room-wide improvement claim.
observations.semantic_recognizability: Mismatched appliance doors, sheet metal and timber identify a Scavenger repair shop overall; the bright cog adds a mild Clockwork association.
observations.silhouette_quality: The rear-set canopy exposes more of the front bay close up, but the 64-inch view remains small and roof-heavy.
observations.surface_variation: Large color areas remain visible in the close render, but fine wear does not materially transfer to the gameplay camera.
observations.technical_integration: Godot 4.7.2 imported and rendered the candidate through the review-only production path with 10 meshes, 10 surfaces and 107,784 triangles.

close_inspection.evidence: The work bay is clearer close up, but the finish and small joins remain below the approved concept and the target craft level.

edge_treatment.evidence: Close captures show eased appliance corners, rolled roof edges and softened timber edges.

hardware.evidence: Roof rivets and appliance hardware exist, but their small forms do not read clearly at the gameplay camera.

joins.evidence: The rear-set roof edge lands on a bearer carried by posts, with side braces providing a readable load path.

manufacturing_detail.evidence: The bench and shelves are easier to see close up, but small hand tools and salvaged details still collapse at settlement distance.

material_response.evidence: The close production render separates weathered timber, enamel and galvanized roofing under the current lighting.

surface_variation.evidence: Broad baked patina creates larger enamel and metal variation close up, though it is subdued at gameplay distance.

thickness.evidence: Roof sheets, appliance panels, drawer fronts and timber members show layered thickness in the close production render.

neutral_viewer_realism.evidence: The close view is coherent but remains visibly stylized and below the approved concept in material richness and crafted detail.

photo_character.evidence: The approved ArtBrief has no photographic source requirement or reference image.

visual_transfer_diagnosis.corrective_action: Backlog this target episode at attempt three. A future new target episode should test a stronger game-scale work-bay massing and remove the residual Clockwork cog cue.
